tagline: Along the north shore of the Pend Oreille to Sandpoint.
intro: From the Washington line at Oldtown, US 2 follows the north shore of the Pend Oreille River east through Priest River and Laclede to Sandpoint, on Lake Pend Oreille. It is the southern leg of the International Selkirk Loop.

The Kalispel and Pend d'Oreille people crossed the river at Seneacquoteen, Salish for deep water crossing, in canoes of white pine bark. In 1863 prospectors bound for the British Columbia gold fields came the same way, and a ferry ran from Laclede for nearly a hundred years, until 1957.

moments.title: Oldtown
moments.text: When the railroad depot burned in 1894 it was rebuilt across the line in Washington, Newport moved with it, and the town left behind in Idaho became Oldtown.

moments.title: Albeni Falls Dam
moments.text: The Corps of Engineers built the dam between 1951 and 1955 over the falls named for Albeni Poirier, a French immigrant who settled here in 1887.

moments.title: Dover
moments.text: After its Laclede mill burned, the lumber company in 1922 moved the whole mill town up the river to Dover, more than 50 buildings on barges, with nothing but winches and horses.
